title: trio-sdk stream connector refactor: deprecate legacy session shim and add adaptive retry profiles
author: Ava Chen
release_notes: Introduce a single StreamAdapter abstraction across Python/TypeScript/Go; deprecate legacy session shim with a compatibility layer; add adaptive retry profiles and a default idle heartbeat to reduce reconnect churn. SDKs bumped: python 2.8.0, typescript 1.13.0, go 1.6.2.
description:
Context: Multiple teams reported inconsistent streaming ergonomics and frequent reconnects for low-throughput long-lived streams. This PR introduces a small, lightweight StreamAdapter abstraction in the redwood monorepo that standardizes backpressure and reauth/reauth-shim behavior across SDKs, plus a set of adaptive retry profiles aimed at reducing noisy reconnects for typical PLG and enterprise workloads.

Summary of changes and rationale (single continuous description): Commits: - Add core/stream/adapter with StreamAdapter interface, TTL-based idle heartbeat, and adaptive retry profile registry (commit: add-stream-adapter-core) - Implement compatibility shim that proxies previously-exported session_shim API to StreamAdapter while emitting deprecation warnings (commit: compat/deprecate-session-shim) - Python SDK: replace legacy SessionShim with PyStreamAdapter, expose ergonomic async iterator for chunked streaming, add tests and type hints, bump version to 2.8.0 (commit: sdk-python/adapter-and-iterator) - TypeScript SDK: implement StreamAdapter facade, normalize backpressure signals to a shared set of events, update stream consumer docs and examples, bump patch to 1.13.0 (commit: sdk-ts/stream-facade) - Go SDK: introduce small stream connector and SessionFactory to reduce token handoff complexity, add integration tests, bump module to 1.6.2 (commit: sdk-go/connector-sessionfactory) - Docs and changelog: update streaming guide, migration notes, and SDK release notes (commit: docs/streaming-migration) - Tests: add e2e scenario that simulates low tokens-per-minute long-lived consumers, unit tests for adaptive profiles and heartbeat (commit: test/stream-adapter-e2e)

Files touched (high level): - core/stream/adapter.py (new) - core/stream/compat_shim.py (new) - sdk/python/redwood/streaming/adapter.py (updated) - sdk/python/tests/test_stream_adapter.py (new) - sdk/typescript/src/stream/adapter.ts (new) - sdk/typescript/examples/stream-heartbeat.md (new) - sdk/go/stream/connector.go (new) - sdk/go/session/factory.go (new) - docs/streaming/migration.md (updated) - sdk/*/CHANGELOG.md (updated)

Motivation: The effort unifies a number of small behavioral differences that caused callers to implement bespoke retry and reconnect logic. Standardizing reduces duplicated code in customer applications and makes telemetry meaningful across languages.

Key design points: - StreamAdapter centralizes three responsibilities: backpressure normalization (pause/resume semantics), token lifecycle/reauth hooks, and an optional idle heartbeat to keep long-lived KV caches warm. - Adaptive retry profiles are pluggable and tuned for three workload buckets (interactive low-latency, batch high-throughput, long-lived low-volume). Profiles are conservative by default to avoid aggressive reconnect storms. - The compat shim provides a deprecation window (two releases) with telemetry so customers can migrate at their cadence without outages.

Review summary and conversation highlights: - Diego: "Nice consolidation. Please add a small benchmark showing end-to-end token-per-second reduction for long-lived streams." Author reply: "Added a micro-benchmark in test/bench/stream_heartbeat_bench.py and included results in the PR description; numbers show ~22% fewer reconnects in the long-lived profile." - Priya (request changes): "The TypeScript backpressure signal mapping needs clearer docs; also ensure that pause() is idempotent across consumers." Author reply: "Clarified adapter.ts comments, added a unit test ensuring idempotency, and included a short example in examples/stream-heartbeat.md." - Evan: "Can we avoid changing the public constructor signature for the Go connector?" Author reply: "We introduced a SessionFactory to preserve the older signature; updated README and left a TODO for the next major where we'll consider a cleaner API."

CI and checks: - Unit tests: pass (python/ts/go) - Integration e2e: pass on linux-amd64 - Lint: ts/py linters pass, go vet clean - Flaky test rerun: one intermittent TS test flaked on first run, re-run succeeded

Outcome: - Merge method: squash and merge - Changelog: SDK versions bumped (python 2.8.0, typescript 1.13.0, go 1.6.2) - Migration: Added docs/streaming/migration.md with a 2-step migration path and example code in each SDK - Rollout: feature toggled via STREAM_ADAPTER=true for 3 weeks before defaulting to true

Notes for maintainers: - Deprecation telemetry emits event: stream.session_shim.deprecated; monitor for adoption. - The compat shim logs a single WARN per process on construction to surface older usages. - If teams want to revert, flip STREAM_ADAPTER=false and roll back the SDK consumer to prior pinned versions.

Related work: ENG-1764 (streaming observability), ENG-1820 (kv-cache keepalive), SUP-874 (customer-reported reconnect storms).
